EU 2024/1987 point 3.6.11.3 'husked rice' (2.0 mg/kg, product as placed on market, a dry cereal at roughly 12-14 % moisture) is neither product-adjacent nor basis-adjacent to wet, as-consumed canned tuna and canned fish (drained fish content), and the same instrument's wet-basis rows all sit far lower: 'baby food except juices' 0.50 mg/kg (point 3.6.15, as placed on market, a category that includes meat- and fish-based baby foods and is the only EU nickel row whose scope contains fish), fruiting vegetables 0.40, brassica and leafy vegetables 0.50, root/tuber/bulb vegetables 0.90 and legume vegetables 1.0 (wet weight). The husked-rice row is in force (applies from 2026-07-01) but is not the nearest same-basis sovereign instrument; the nearer one is the baby-food row at 500 ug/kg (Switzerland VHK mirrors it at 500 as consumed), so the read-across as claimed is refuted and the blind value is 500.

The register holds no sovereign nickel ML for fish, crustaceans, molluscs, cephalopods or any animal tissue (its 93 nickel rows are EU 2024/1987 and Swiss VHK plant-food rows, GB 2762-2025 hydrogenated oils, drinking and bottled water, cosmetics, fertiliser, biosolids, toy-migration, food-contact-migration and ICH Q3D rows), so a read-across is unavoidable, but husked rice is not the nearest same-basis instrument: within the same regulation the wet-weight rows (fruiting vegetables 400, brassica and leafy vegetables 500, root, tuber and bulb vegetables 900) and the as-placed-on-market finished-food row 'baby food except juices' 500 (eu2024_ni_babyfood_500), whose legal scope includes meat- and fish-based foods, are nearer in moisture, basis and product form to wet animal tissue eaten as consumed than a roughly 12 percent-moisture grain at the second-loosest cereal level.
